verdict.rationale: Copilot's own agents do Git and PR work. The cloud agent works independently in the background, can be told via @copilot to make changes on an existing pull request, and Copilot Chat can work with pull requests through GitHub's first-party MCP server. However, no evidence explicitly documents the specific steps of staging, writing commit messages, creating branches or opening new PRs. Missing for 10: explicit docs for staging changes, generating commit messages, creating branches, opening new pull requests, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent stage changes, write commit messages, create branches, and open pull requests

citations.quote: Mention `@copilot` in a comment on an existing pull request to ask it to make changes.
GitHub Copilot can work independently in the background to complete tasks, just like a human developer.
interact with repositories, issues, pull requests, and other GitHub features, directly from Copilot Chat in your IDE
review changes, and merge completed work
